findings.checklist_item: Scope AC-1/AC-2 to the visibility the fix actually delivers (log-stream + synchronous/handler-attached callers, asserted via caplog), and state explicitly that delivering the warning into the async/MCP caller's channel is RC-3 and out of this ticket's scope.
evidence: AC-1: 'a rejected auto-push is surfaced to the writing CALLER rather than failing silently'
AC-2: 'asserts the caller SEES it -- not a mock's call count'
RC-3: 'Library embedders get only the NullHandler'; 'Under MCP the warning goes to the server's stderr, never into the tool result the writing agent reads'
Fix mechanism is logger.warning at push.py:176/296; the test is a caplog assertion ('the surfaced warning names the reason')
findings.finding: The chosen mechanism (a richer logger.warning) achieves LOG-stream visibility, but the ticket's own RC-3 evidence establishes the warning never reaches the writing caller on the async path (stderr=DEVNULL, push.py:128-141), for library embedders (NullHandler, __init__.py:131), or under MCP (server stderr, not the tool result). With RC-3 explicitly split out of scope, AC-1 ('surfaced to the writing CALLER') and AC-2 ('the caller SEES it') overreach what fix #1-#3 can deliver on those paths — they are only satisfiable via log capture on the synchronous/handler-attached path.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria bullets 1-2; FIX PLAN vs. PROVEN ROOT CAUSE RC-3
scenarios: sync.push=async: push runs in a detached Popen with stderr=DEVNULL — the improved warning is discarded entirely
An MCP-hosted agent write: warning lands on server stderr, not in the tool result the agent reads
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC-1/AC-2 to 'a rejected auto-push emits a warning naming the git reason and the unpushed-commit count on the synchronous push path (asserted via caplog); routing that warning into the async/MCP caller channel is tracked as RC-3 and out of scope here.'

findings.checklist_item: Specify that the backlog-count step guards for a missing/absent origin/tickets (mirror fsck.py:402's rev-parse --verify) and defines the warning wording when the remote ref does not yet exist.
evidence: fsck.py:418-422 counts only after fsck.py:402 verifies the remote ref exists and 417 confirms remote is an ancestor
In push.py the fetch that materializes origin/tickets is at push.py:198, INSIDE the non-ff reconcile loop — a terminal policy rejection (fix #1) exits before reaching it
Plan gives no guard/fallback for an absent-or-stale origin/tickets when emitting the count on the new terminal path
findings.finding: Fix #3 computes the backlog as origin/tickets..HEAD, but the NEW terminal policy-rejection path added by fix #1 can fire on a FIRST push, before the reconcile-loop fetch (push.py:198) ever ran, so origin/tickets may not exist yet. rev-list against a missing ref fails and the count is undefined. The existing PUSH_PENDING site guards this exact case (fsck.py:402 `rev-parse --verify remote_ref` before counting); the plan does not state the new path will guard it.
findings.location: FIX PLAN item 3 ('Include the unpushed-commit count (origin/tickets..HEAD)')
scenarios: A brand-new tickets branch whose very first push is declined by push protection (GH013) — the token 'hook declined' routes to the new terminal path with no origin/tickets yet
findings.suggested_fix: Add to fix #3: 'if origin/tickets does not resolve (first push, ref absent), omit the count or report the full local ahead-of-root count, and never let the count computation raise — the best-effort contract still holds.'
